title: Polynomial unique factorization and prime quotients over a PID
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative principal ideal domain, meaning an integral domain in which every ideal is generated by one element. For $n\geq0$, put $P=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $P$ is a unique factorization domain: every nonzero nonunit has a finite factorization into irreducibles, unique up to order and multiplication by units. Every irreducible $f\in P$ is a prime element, so $(f)$ is a proper prime ideal and $P/(f)$ is an integral domain. Here irreducible means a nonzero nonunit such that in every product expression one factor is a unit; prime means nonzero and not a unit, and dividing a product only if it divides a factor.
